messages:
Samir Patel: Hey team — customer Lotus Labs reported an inbound wire got returned by their bank during overnight settlement. they pasted the bank reply below and asked why.

Priya Rao: Thanks Samir. Can you drop the payment id + last 4 of account? I will open a ticket with treasury.

Samir Patel: payment_id: pay_2026_07_12_0091, amount: 41,250.00 USD, beneficiary: Lotus Labs Inc (redacted), beneficiary_account: 000123456789, beneficiary_routing: 021000021, swift: BOFAUS3NXXX, value_date: 2026-07-12

Samir Patel: Bank response: 
```
RETURNED
Reason code: 016
Message: Invalid account number / format
Bank note: Non-IBAN format expected by correspondent, refused by intermediary
SWIFT: MT103: :72: /REJD/INVALID ACCT FORMAT
```

Marta Lopez: @Samir can you confirm whether this was a cross-border wire? the swift looks domestic (BOFAUS3N) but the beneficiary account has leading zeros, which some correspondents trim.

Samir Patel: It's USD to a US beneficiary — initiated from our EU rails. customer used the account number they have on file (12 digits). the intermediary bank apparently expected 10-digit.

Jules Nguyen: This smells like normalization mismatch between our outbound adapter and the correspondent. we recently enabled the "trim_leading_zeros" normalization for SEPA->US rails. can you paste the raw outbound payload?

Samir Patel: outbound payload (sanitized):
```
{
  "payment_id": "pay_2026_07_12_0091",
  "amount": "41250.00",
  "currency": "USD",
  "beneficiary": {"name": "Lotus Labs Inc","account": "000123456789","routing": "021000021"},
  "instructions": "Invoice 6221",
  "origin_country": "DE"
}
```

Priya Rao: copy. @Jules any known deploy or config change in the adapter that could trim zeros?

Jules Nguyen: There was a hotfix 2026-07-11 that adjusted account normalization for certain correspondent chains. it should only apply to accounts labelled as IBANs, but looks like our origin_country header was misread and we applied trimming.

Payments Bot: Payment pay_2026_07_12_0091 marked as RETURNED by correspondent 2026-07-12T03:14:12Z - reason: Invalid account format. Ticket auto-created: #TREAS-9812.

Marta Lopez: Next steps: 1) confirm whether customer-provided account actually requires leading zeros (ask customer to verify with beneficiary bank). 2) Re-run same payload without trim (or restore original account field) and resubmit as a new payment. 3) Escalate to correspondent with MT103 copy and ask for exact expected format. 4) Patch our adapter to apply trimming only when origin indicates IBAN or when bank metadata says so.

Priya Rao: I'll ping the customer for verification and share the MT103. drafting msg: "We see the return code 016 (invalid account format). Can you confirm the exact account format your bank expects (10 vs 12 digits) and if there are any leading zeros in their systems? Also please confirm the bank's full BIC/SWIFT and any intermediary bank details."

Samir Patel: Sent that to Lotus support. they replied: "Our operations confirmed account is 000123456789 and their bank uses 12-digit internal account numbers. they flagged correspondent refused because they expected 10-digit clearing acct. they suggested payment should route via intermediary BIC ABCDUS33XXX."

Jules Nguyen: ok. while customer waits, i'll reprocess a test using the raw account (no trimming) and route via suggested intermediary BIC. i'll create a replay payment with tag test_replay_0091.

Jules Nguyen: (after test) Test replay failed at correspondent with same 016. the MT103 shows our adapter still inserting trimmed_account: "123456789" in the <Acct> element. looks like the normalization runs in the message renderer step after we assemble the JSON.

Priya Rao: can we hotfix to bypass trimming for this payment path? impact window small but needs review.

Jules Nguyen: yes — patch ready. pushing canary to staging now. change: skip trim when origin_country != "US" and beneficiary_country == "US" AND customer_flag_force_no_trim set. will add a backend flag to support one-off fixes.

Payments Bot: Deploy started: payments/adapter v3.4.7-canary by jnguyen at 2026-07-12T10:05:00Z

Marta Lopez: please also attach the correspondent's refusal logs to TREAS-9812 and ask for escalation path. we need explicit doc from their ops saying which fields they consider authoritative.

Samir Patel: Customer replied and provided intermediary BIC and a confirmation screenshot from their bank showing account = 000123456789 and "no trimming" requirement. forwarded to TREAS-9812.

Jules Nguyen: Can confirm canary fixed the renderer bug in staging. replay with original account and intermediary BIC succeeded in staging routing. will roll out patch to canary prod for the affected mirror region tonight and then to prod if green.

Priya Rao: great — i'll mark customer informed and keep them updated. flagging as escalated with high priority until funds remake/settlement completes. :white_check_mark:

Marta Lopez: closing loop checklist: - TREAS ticket updated with MT103 and bank screenshot - code patch merged and canary deployed - customer notified - monitoring alert for similar return codes created (rule: payments.returned.reason==016 AND origin_country!=beneficiary_country)

Samir Patel: thanks everyone. will follow up when remittance completes. :thumbsup:
